why: A third dataset draw, seed 3, and it is not chosen -- whatever it says stands. ci-90 moved the seed from 1 to 2 and returned two results that point opposite ways. The lambda 0.9 spike collapsed: the value policy went from 0.6625 against search-4 on seed 1 to 0.0975 on seed 2, win rate 9.5% with an interval of 6.8% to 12.2%, so ci-88 beating search-4 was one lucky fit rather than a property of that lambda. Changing which 1000 matches are fitted on moved that number by 56 points, which is larger than every lambda effect measured this week put together. Meanwhile the clone cleared all four bars for the first time in the loop's history: 0.79875 against Greedy against its usual 0.725, 0.9875 against Random, 0.5775 against search-4 with a win rate of 57.2% and an interval of 53.0% to 61.5%, and 0.53625 against the committed champion ci-69 with an interval from 0.51473. That is the opposite shape from ci-88 -- it beats Greedy better than any policy before it and loses to nothing -- but only a seed changed, and the evaluation runs on FIXED benchmark seeds, so trying dataset seeds until one scores well is selection on the test set. The value policy in that same run proves a seed can swing a headline by 56 points. So the clone has not been shown to be better, only to score better on one draw, which is what ci-88 looked like a few hours earlier. This turn takes seed 3 with everything else held: if the clone is near 0.8 against Greedy again, seed 1 was the unlucky draw and the clone genuinely improved; if it falls back near 0.725, both ci-88 and ci-90 were draws and the run-to-run spread of this pipeline is wider than anything it has been asked to measure. Do not commit a model on a seed picked for its score. Still open: reading the capped matches apart from the decided ones, a second independent opponent that is not the teacher, and the nonlinear baseline ADR 0048 left on the table.
